postgresql_otel-backend-buffer-writes.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Backend buffer writes high
postgresql_otel-backend-buffer-writes.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Buffers written by backend (not bgwriter) indicate background writer cannot keep up
| WHERE postgresql.bgwriter.buffers.writes IS NOT NULL AND attributes.source == "backend"
| EVAL writes_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.bgwriter.buffers.writes)
| STATS backend_writes = SUM(writes_val) BY service.instance.id
// Threshold: > 100 buffers in window; adjust based on checkpoint frequency
| WHERE backend_writes > 100

postgresql_otel-bgwriter-maxwritten.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Bgwriter maxwritten stops
postgresql_otel-bgwriter-maxwritten.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Bgwriter stopped because it wrote too many buffers; indicates write pressure
| WHERE postgresql.bgwriter.maxwritten IS NOT NULL
| EVAL maxwritten_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.bgwriter.maxwritten)
| WHERE maxwritten_val > 0
| STATS maxwritten_count = SUM(maxwritten_val) BY service.instance.id
| WHERE maxwritten_count > 0

postgresql_otel-connection-utilization-h.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Connection utilization high

postgresql_otel-deadlocks-detected.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Deadlocks detected
postgresql_otel-deadlocks-detected.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Deadlocks are database-level monotonic counter; any increase indicates concurrency issues
| WHERE postgresql.deadlocks IS NOT NULL
| EVAL deadlocks_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.deadlocks)
| WHERE deadlocks_val > 0
// Group by instance and database for targeted alerting
| STATS deadlock_count = SUM(deadlocks_val) BY service.instance.id, postgresql.database.name
| WHERE deadlock_count > 0

postgresql_otel-exclusive-lock-contentio.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Exclusive lock contention
postgresql_otel-exclusive-lock-contentio.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Locks by mode; ExclusiveLock and AccessExclusiveLock indicate contention
| WHERE postgresql.database.locks IS NOT NULL
| WHERE attributes.mode IN ("ExclusiveLock", "AccessExclusiveLock")
| STATS lock_count = SUM(postgresql.database.locks) BY service.instance.id, attributes.mode
// Threshold: > 5 exclusive locks; adjust for your workload
| WHERE lock_count > 5

postgresql_otel-high-rollback-rate.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] High rollback rate

postgresql_otel-high-sequential-scans.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] High sequential scans
postgresql_otel-high-sequential-scans.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Sequential scans on large tables suggest missing indexes; table-level metric (production)
| WHERE postgresql.sequential_scans IS NOT NULL
| EVAL seq_scans_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.sequential_scans)
| WHERE seq_scans_val > 0
| STATS seq_scan_count = SUM(seq_scans_val) BY service.instance.id, postgresql.database.name
// Threshold: > 1000 scans in window; adjust for table count and workload
| WHERE seq_scan_count > 1000

postgresql_otel-high-temp-io.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] High temp I/O volume
postgresql_otel-high-temp-io.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Temp I/O (bytes written to temp files) indicates memory-constrained workloads
| WHERE postgresql.temp.io IS NOT NULL
| EVAL temp_io_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.temp.io)
| WHERE temp_io_val > 0
| STATS temp_io_bytes = SUM(temp_io_val) BY service.instance.id, postgresql.database.name
// Threshold: 100 MB in window; adjust for your scrape interval and expected load
| WHERE temp_io_bytes > 104857600

postgresql_otel-long-checkpoint-duration.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Long checkpoint duration
postgresql_otel-long-checkpoint-duration.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Checkpoint duration (sync + write) is server-level with attributes.type
| WHERE postgresql.bgwriter.duration IS NOT NULL
| EVAL duration_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.bgwriter.duration)
| STATS total_duration_ms = SUM(duration_val) BY service.instance.id
// Threshold: 30 seconds total in window; adjust for your checkpoint frequency
| WHERE total_duration_ms > 30000

postgresql_otel-long-running-queries.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Long-running queries
postgresql_otel-long-running-queries.esql:
FROM logs-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Active query samples from pg_stat_activity; total_exec_time is real-time execution ms
| WHERE event_name == "db.server.query_sample"
| WHERE attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time IS NOT NULL
// Threshold: queries running > 5 minutes (300000 ms); adjust for your SLA
| WHERE attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time > 300000
| KEEP service.instance.id, attributes.db.namespace, attributes.db.query.text, attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time, attributes.postgresql.pid
| SORT attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time DESC
| LIMIT 20

postgresql_otel-low-buffer-hit-ratio.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Low buffer hit ratio
postgresql_otel-low-buffer-hit-ratio.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Buffer hit ratio = blks_hit / (blks_hit + blks_read); healthy is > 99%
| WHERE postgresql.blks_hit IS NOT NULL OR postgresql.blks_read IS NOT NULL
| EVAL hit_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.blks_hit), read_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.blks_read)
| STATS blks_hit = SUM(hit_val), blks_read = SUM(read_val) BY service.instance.id, postgresql.database.name
| WHERE (blks_hit + blks_read) > 1000
// Hit ratio below 99% indicates cache pressure; adjust threshold as needed
| EVAL hit_ratio_pct = ROUND(blks_hit / (blks_hit + blks_read) * 100.0, 2)
| WHERE hit_ratio_pct < 99.0

postgresql_otel-queries-waiting-on-locks.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Queries waiting on locks
postgresql_otel-queries-waiting-on-locks.esql:
FROM logs-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Query samples with Lock wait event type indicate blocked queries
| WHERE event_name == "db.server.query_sample"
| WHERE attributes.postgresql.wait_event_type == "Lock"
| WHERE attributes.postgresql.wait_event != "" AND attributes.postgresql.wait_event IS NOT NULL
| STATS blocked_count = COUNT(*) BY service.instance.id, attributes.db.namespace
| WHERE blocked_count > 0

postgresql_otel-slow-top-queries.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Slow top queries
postgresql_otel-slow-top-queries.esql:
FROM logs-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Top query stats from pg_stat_statements; total_exec_time is delta per scrape
| WHERE event_name == "db.server.top_query"
| WHERE attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time IS NOT NULL AND attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time > 0
// Threshold: total exec time > 10 seconds in window (delta); tune for scrape interval
| WHERE attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time > 10000
| KEEP service.instance.id, attributes.db.namespace, attributes.db.query.text, attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time, attributes.postgresql.calls
| SORT attributes.postgresql.total_exec_time DESC
| LIMIT 20

postgresql_otel-temp-files-created.name: [PostgreSQL OTel] Temp files created
postgresql_otel-temp-files-created.esql:
FROM metrics-postgresqlreceiver.otel-*
// Temp file creation indicates queries spilling to disk (insufficient work_mem or poor query plans)
| WHERE postgresql.temp_files IS NOT NULL
| EVAL temp_files_val = TO_DOUBLE(postgresql.temp_files)
| WHERE temp_files_val > 0
| STATS temp_file_count = SUM(temp_files_val) BY service.instance.id, postgresql.database.name
| WHERE temp_file_count > 0

rabbitmq_otel-disk-alarm.name: [RabbitMQ OTel] Disk alarm triggered
rabbitmq_otel-disk-alarm.esql:
FROM metrics-rabbitmqreceiver.otel-default
// Disk alarm: when triggered (1), publishing is halted
// Requires node-level metrics enabled in receiver config
| WHERE metrics.rabbitmq.node.disk_free_alarm IS NOT NULL
  AND metrics.rabbitmq.node.disk_free_alarm > 0
| STATS alarm_count = COUNT(*)
  BY resource.attributes.rabbitmq.node.name
| WHERE alarm_count > 0

rabbitmq_otel-high-ready-queue-depth.name: [RabbitMQ OTel] High ready queue depth
rabbitmq_otel-high-ready-queue-depth.esql:
FROM metrics-rabbitmqreceiver.otel-default
// Filter to ready messages (waiting for delivery)
| WHERE attributes.state == "ready"
  AND metrics.rabbitmq.message.current IS NOT NULL
// Get max ready count per queue in the time window
| STATS ready_count = MAX(metrics.rabbitmq.message.current)
  BY resource.attributes.rabbitmq.queue.name,
     resource.attributes.rabbitmq.vhost.name,
     resource.attributes.rabbitmq.node.name
// Alert threshold: adjust 1000 to tune for expected backlog size
| WHERE ready_count > 1000
| SORT ready_count DESC
| LIMIT 20

rabbitmq_otel-high-unacknowledged-messag.name: [RabbitMQ OTel] High unacknowledged message count
rabbitmq_otel-high-unacknowledged-messag.esql:
FROM metrics-rabbitmqreceiver.otel-default
// Unacknowledged: delivered but not yet acked; buildup indicates consumer issues
| WHERE attributes.state == "unacknowledged"
  AND metrics.rabbitmq.message.current IS NOT NULL
| STATS unack_count = MAX(metrics.rabbitmq.message.current)
  BY resource.attributes.rabbitmq.queue.name,
     resource.attributes.rabbitmq.vhost.name,
     resource.attributes.rabbitmq.node.name
// Alert threshold: adjust 500 to tune for consumer processing expectations
| WHERE unack_count > 500
| SORT unack_count DESC
| LIMIT 20

rabbitmq_otel-memory-alarm.name: [RabbitMQ OTel] Memory alarm triggered
rabbitmq_otel-memory-alarm.esql:
FROM metrics-rabbitmqreceiver.otel-default
// Memory alarm: when triggered (1), producers are blocked
// Requires node-level metrics enabled in receiver config
| WHERE metrics.rabbitmq.node.mem_alarm IS NOT NULL
  AND metrics.rabbitmq.node.mem_alarm > 0
| STATS alarm_count = COUNT(*)
  BY resource.attributes.rabbitmq.node.name
| WHERE alarm_count > 0

rabbitmq_otel-queue-zero-consumers.name: [RabbitMQ OTel] Queue with zero consumers and ready messages
rabbitmq_otel-queue-zero-consumers.esql:
FROM metrics-rabbitmqreceiver.otel-default
| WHERE resource.attributes.rabbitmq.queue.name IS NOT NULL
// Aggregate ready messages and consumer count per queue
| STATS
    ready_count = MAX(metrics.rabbitmq.message.current) WHERE attributes.state == "ready",
    consumer_count = MAX(metrics.rabbitmq.consumer.count)
  BY resource.attributes.rabbitmq.queue.name,
     resource.attributes.rabbitmq.vhost.name,
     resource.attributes.rabbitmq.node.name
// Alert when queue has messages but no consumers
| WHERE ready_count > 0 AND COALESCE(consumer_count, TO_LONG(0)) == 0
| SORT ready_count DESC
| LIMIT 20

redis_otel-high-eviction-rate.name: [Redis OTel] High eviction rate

redis_otel-memory-fragmentation-swapping.name: [Redis OTel] Memory fragmentation indicates swapping
redis_otel-memory-fragmentation-swapping.esql:
FROM metrics-redisreceiver.otel-*
| WHERE data_stream.dataset == "redisreceiver.otel"
  AND redis.memory.fragmentation_ratio IS NOT NULL
// Fragmentation ratio < 1.0 means RSS < used memory: Redis is swapping to disk
| STATS avg_frag = AVG(redis.memory.fragmentation_ratio)
  BY server.address, server.port
| WHERE avg_frag < 1.0
| SORT avg_frag ASC

redis_otel-memory-near-max.name: [Redis OTel] Memory approaching maxmemory
redis_otel-memory-near-max.esql:
FROM metrics-redisreceiver.otel-*
| WHERE data_stream.dataset == "redisreceiver.otel"
  AND redis.memory.used IS NOT NULL
  AND redis.maxmemory IS NOT NULL
  AND redis.maxmemory > 0
// Used memory as percentage of maxmemory
| STATS used = MAX(redis.memory.used),
        max_mem = MAX(redis.maxmemory)
  BY server.address, server.port
| EVAL usage_pct = ROUND(used / max_mem * 100.0, 2)
// Alert when usage exceeds 90%; adjust threshold as needed
| WHERE usage_pct > 90.0
| SORT usage_pct DESC

redis_otel-rejected-connections.name: [Redis OTel] Rejected connections
redis_otel-rejected-connections.esql:
TS metrics-redisreceiver.otel-*
| WHERE redis.connections.rejected IS NOT NULL
// Counter: use INCREASE to get rejections over the time window
| STATS rejected = SUM(INCREASE(redis.connections.rejected))
  BY server.address, server.port
// Alert when any instance rejected at least one connection (maxclients reached)
| WHERE rejected > 0
| SORT rejected DESC

redis_otel-replicas-disconnected.name: [Redis OTel] Primary has no connected replicas

redisenterprise_otel-certificate-expirin.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] TLS certificate expiring soon

redisenterprise_otel-database-down.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Database down

redisenterprise_otel-database-high-laten.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Database high latency

redisenterprise_otel-database-memory-cri.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Database memory utilization critical
redisenterprise_otel-database-memory-cri.esql:
FROM metrics-redisenterprise.otel-default
| WHERE bdb_used_memory IS NOT NULL
    AND bdb_memory_limit IS NOT NULL
    AND bdb_memory_limit > 0
| STATS
    avg_used = AVG(bdb_used_memory),
    avg_limit = AVG(bdb_memory_limit)
  BY bdb, cluster
| EVAL utilization_pct = ROUND(avg_used / avg_limit * 100, 2)
// Alert when memory utilization exceeds 90%
// For non-caching workloads, exceeding the limit causes OOM rejections
// For caching workloads with eviction policies, higher utilization is expected —
// consider raising this threshold or disabling for cache-only databases
| WHERE utilization_pct > 90
| SORT utilization_pct DESC

redisenterprise_otel-database-unexpected.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Database unexpected key evictions

redisenterprise_otel-listener-auth-error.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Authentication failures detected

redisenterprise_otel-node-down.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Node down

redisenterprise_otel-node-high-cpu.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Node CPU saturation
redisenterprise_otel-node-high-cpu.esql:
FROM metrics-redisenterprise.otel-default
| WHERE node_cpu_user IS NOT NULL
    AND node_cpu_system IS NOT NULL
    AND node_cpu_idle IS NOT NULL
| STATS
    avg_user = AVG(node_cpu_user),
    avg_system = AVG(node_cpu_system),
    avg_idle = AVG(node_cpu_idle)
  BY node, cluster
| EVAL total = avg_user + avg_system + avg_idle
| EVAL cpu_util_pct = ROUND((avg_user + avg_system) / total * 100, 2)
// Alert when CPU utilization exceeds 85%
// CPU is computed as (user + system) / (user + system + idle)
// Sustained high CPU may indicate the node needs scaling or workload rebalancing
// Adjust threshold based on your capacity planning targets
| WHERE total > 0 AND cpu_util_pct > 85
| SORT cpu_util_pct DESC

redisenterprise_otel-node-low-memory.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Node free memory low

redisenterprise_otel-node-storage-low.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Node storage running low
redisenterprise_otel-node-storage-low.esql:
FROM metrics-redisenterprise.otel-default
| WHERE node_persistent_storage_avail IS NOT NULL
    OR node_ephemeral_storage_avail IS NOT NULL
| STATS
    avg_persistent = AVG(node_persistent_storage_avail),
    avg_ephemeral = AVG(node_ephemeral_storage_avail)
  BY node, cluster
| EVAL persistent_gb = ROUND(avg_persistent / 1073741824, 2)
| EVAL ephemeral_gb = ROUND(avg_ephemeral / 1073741824, 2)
// Alert when available storage drops below 5 GB on either volume
// Persistent storage holds AOF/RDB snapshots; exhaustion prevents persistence
// Ephemeral storage holds temp files and logs; exhaustion can crash processes
// Adjust thresholds based on your node's total disk capacity
| WHERE (persistent_gb IS NOT NULL AND persistent_gb < 5)
    OR (ephemeral_gb IS NOT NULL AND ephemeral_gb < 5)
| SORT persistent_gb ASC

redisenterprise_otel-proxy-fd-saturation.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Proxy file descriptor saturation
redisenterprise_otel-proxy-fd-saturation.esql:
FROM metrics-redisenterprise.otel-default
| WHERE dmcproxy_process_open_fds IS NOT NULL
    AND dmcproxy_process_max_fds IS NOT NULL
    AND dmcproxy_process_max_fds > 0
| STATS
    avg_open = AVG(dmcproxy_process_open_fds),
    avg_max = AVG(dmcproxy_process_max_fds)
  BY proxy, node, cluster
| EVAL fd_util_pct = ROUND(avg_open / avg_max * 100, 2)
// Alert when file descriptor utilization exceeds 80%
// The DMC proxy uses one FD per client connection; exhaustion rejects new connections
// Investigate connection leaks, increase system ulimits, or add connection pooling
| WHERE fd_util_pct > 80
| SORT fd_util_pct DESC

redisenterprise_otel-shard-connection-sa.name: [Redis Enterprise OTel] Shard connection saturation
redisenterprise_otel-shard-connection-sa.esql:
FROM metrics-redisenterprise.otel-default
| WHERE redis_connected_clients IS NOT NULL
    AND redis_maxclients IS NOT NULL
    AND redis_maxclients > 0
| STATS
    avg_clients = AVG(redis_connected_clients),
    avg_max = AVG(redis_maxclients)
  BY redis, bdb, node, cluster
| EVAL conn_util_pct = ROUND(avg_clients / avg_max * 100, 2)
// Alert when connection utilization exceeds 80%
// Reaching maxclients causes new connections to be rejected
// Investigate client connection pooling or increase maxclients
| WHERE conn_util_pct > 80
| SORT conn_util_pct DESC

supabase_otel-supavisor-pool-exhaustion.name: [Supabase OTel] Supavisor pool exhausted
supabase_otel-supavisor-pool-exhaustion.esql:
TS metrics-supabase.metrics.otel-*
// Supavisor gauges are per tenant / mode / node, so SUM() across series gives the pool
// totals for the tenant. Projects without the shared pooler emit none of these series,
// so the query returns no rows rather than a false breach.
| STATS
    `Checked Out` = SUM(LAST_OVER_TIME(supavisor_pool_connections_checked_out)),
    `Idle` = SUM(LAST_OVER_TIME(supavisor_pool_connections_idle)),
    `Active Connections` = SUM(LAST_OVER_TIME(supavisor_connections_active))
  BY resource.attributes.supabase_project_ref, attributes.tenant, attributes.mode
| EVAL `Pool Size` = `Checked Out` + `Idle`
| WHERE `Pool Size` > 0
| EVAL `Checked Out %` = ROUND(`Checked Out` / `Pool Size` * 100, 1)
// 95% of the open pool checked out. Pool Size is derived from live connections, so a very
// small pool crosses this easily; raise the Pool Size floor if that proves noisy.
| WHERE `Checked Out %` >= 95
| EVAL alert_instance = CONCAT(resource.attributes.supabase_project_ref, " / ", attributes.tenant, " / ", attributes.mode)
| SORT `Checked Out %` DESC

temporal_otel-high-activity-failure-rate.name: [Temporal OTel] High Activity Task Failure Rate
temporal_otel-high-activity-failure-rate.esql:
TS metrics-temporal.cloud_metrics.otel-*
| STATS fail_rate = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(metrics.temporal_cloud_v1_activity_task_fail_count)),
        success_rate = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(metrics.temporal_cloud_v1_activity_success_count))
    BY attributes.temporal_namespace, attributes.temporal_task_queue
// Compute total attempts; require minimum throughput to avoid low-volume noise
| EVAL fail_rate = CASE(fail_rate IS NULL, 0.0, fail_rate),
        success_rate = CASE(success_rate IS NULL, 0.0, success_rate)
| EVAL fail_plus_success = fail_rate + success_rate
| WHERE fail_plus_success > 0.1
// Compute failure rate as a percentage; CASE treats a missing fail_rate as 0
| EVAL fail_ratio_pct = ROUND(fail_rate / fail_plus_success * 100.0, 2)
// Alert when failure rate exceeds 10%; tune this threshold for your workload
| WHERE fail_ratio_pct > 10
| SORT fail_ratio_pct DESC
| LIMIT 20

temporal_otel-open-workflows-anomaly.name: [Temporal OTel] Namespace Open Workflow Count Anomaly

    BY attributes.temporal_namespace

temporal_otel-task-queue-backlog.name: [Temporal OTel] Task Queue Backlog Growing

temporal_otel-workflow-timeout-rate.name: [Temporal OTel] Workflow Timeout Rate Elevated
temporal_otel-workflow-timeout-rate.esql:
TS metrics-temporal.cloud_metrics.otel-*
| STATS timeout_rate = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(metrics.temporal_cloud_v1_workflow_timeout_count)),
        success_rate = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(metrics.temporal_cloud_v1_workflow_success_count))
    BY attributes.temporal_namespace, attributes.temporal_task_queue
// workflow_timeout_count only emits when timeouts occur; null rates are excluded
| WHERE timeout_rate > 0.01
// Compute timeout percentage of all workflow closures for context
| EVAL timeout_pct = ROUND(
    timeout_rate /
    (timeout_rate + CASE(success_rate IS NULL, 0.0, success_rate)) * 100.0,
    3)
| SORT timeout_rate DESC
| LIMIT 20

    AND vercel.log.source IN ("lambda", "edge")
| STATS
    total = COUNT(*),
    crashes = COUNT(*) WHERE http.response.status_code == -1
  BY vercel.log.source
// Minimum sample size to avoid noisy alerts on low-traffic sources
| WHERE total > 20
| EVAL crash_rate_pct = ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(crashes) / total * 100.0, 2)
// Alert threshold: crashes are rarer and more severe than generic 5xx responses, so this is set tighter.

vercel_otel-pageview-rate-drop.name: [Vercel OTel] Page view rate drop
vercel_otel-pageview-rate-drop.esql:
FROM logs-vercel.analytics.v2.otel-default
| WHERE deployment.environment.name == "production"
    AND vercel.analytics.event.type == "pageview"
// Split the window in half: "recent" (last 15m) vs "baseline" (previous 15m) to detect a drop within a single evaluation
| EVAL is_recent = CASE(@timestamp >= NOW() - 15 minutes, 1, 0)
| STATS
    recent = SUM(is_recent),
    baseline = SUM(1 - is_recent)
  BY vercel.project.id
// Minimum baseline volume to avoid flagging naturally quiet/low-traffic projects
| WHERE baseline > 5
| EVAL drop_pct = ROUND(100.0 - (TO_DOUBLE(recent) / baseline * 100.0), 2)
// Alert threshold: tune based on expected traffic variance for your project
| WHERE drop_pct > 50.0
| SORT drop_pct DESC
| LIMIT 20

vercel_otel-poor-core-web-vitals-by-rout.name: [Vercel OTel] Poor Core Web Vitals (p75) by route
vercel_otel-poor-core-web-vitals-by-rout.esql:
TS metrics-vercel.speedinsights.v1.otel-default
| WHERE deployment.environment.name == "production"
// Evaluate LCP, INP, and CLS independently per route, then union the results (FORK branches must share a schema)
| FORK
    (WHERE metrics.LCP IS NOT NULL
     | STATS p75 = PERCENTILE(metrics.LCP, 75), samples = COUNT(metrics.LCP) BY route = COALESCE(http.route, url.path)
     // "Poor" threshold per the Web Vitals spec table (milliseconds); adjust to your own SLA if stricter
     | EVAL metric = "LCP", poor_threshold = 4000.0)
    (WHERE metrics.INP IS NOT NULL
     | STATS p75 = PERCENTILE(metrics.INP, 75), samples = COUNT(metrics.INP) BY route = COALESCE(http.route, url.path)
     | EVAL metric = "INP", poor_threshold = 500.0)
    (WHERE metrics.CLS IS NOT NULL
     | STATS p75 = PERCENTILE(metrics.CLS, 75), samples = COUNT(metrics.CLS) BY route = COALESCE(http.route, url.path)
     // CLS is unitless; "poor" threshold per the spec table
     | EVAL metric = "CLS", poor_threshold = 0.25)
// Minimum sample size per route/metric, since Speed Insights data is sampled
| WHERE samples >= 5
| WHERE p75 > poor_threshold
// Combine route + metric into a single grouping key since the rule can only group alerts by one field
| EVAL group_key = CONCAT(route, " - ", metric)
| SORT p75 DESC
| LIMIT 20

vercel_otel-regional-error-rate-skew.name: [Vercel OTel] Regional error rate skew
vercel_otel-regional-error-rate-skew.esql:
FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default
| WHERE deployment.environment.name == "production"
    AND vercel.log.source IN ("lambda", "edge")
    // -1 means the function crashed before returning any response; excluded here
    AND http.response.status_code != -1
| STATS
    total = COUNT(*),
    errors = COUNT(*) WHERE http.response.status_code >= 500
  BY vercel.execution.region
// Minimum sample size per region to avoid noisy alerts on low-traffic regions
| WHERE total > 20
| EVAL region_error_rate_pct = ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(errors) / total * 100.0, 2)
// Regional threshold is set higher than the global 5xx rule (2%) because a single region naturally has
// higher variance with a smaller sample; adjust based on your regional traffic distribution.
| WHERE region_error_rate_pct > 5.0
| SORT region_error_rate_pct DESC
| LIMIT 10

vercel_otel-request-rate-drop.name: [Vercel OTel] Request rate drop (traffic collapse)

| STATS
    recent = SUM(is_recent),
    baseline = SUM(1 - is_recent)
  BY vercel.project.id
// Minimum baseline volume to avoid flagging naturally quiet/low-traffic projects

vercel_otel-sensitive-audit-activity-spi.name: [Vercel OTel] Sensitive audit activity spike by actor
vercel_otel-sensitive-audit-activity-spi.esql:
FROM logs-vercel.auditlog.v1.otel-default
// Fall back through identifying fields since non-user actors (app/system/integration) lack user.* fields
| EVAL actor = COALESCE(user.email, user.name, user.id, vercel.actor.type)
// Sensitive action categories: env var access, drain/webhook config (log exfiltration risk), token issuance,
// team/domain configuration, and project ownership transfers. Extend this list as needed.
| WHERE event_name LIKE "*env-variable*"
    OR event_name LIKE "*drain*"
    OR event_name LIKE "*webhook*"
    OR event_name LIKE "*token*"
    OR event_name LIKE "*team-*"
    OR event_name LIKE "*domain*"
    OR event_name LIKE "*project-transfer*"
| STATS sensitive_events = COUNT(*) BY actor
// Alert threshold: tune based on your team's normal operational volume of sensitive actions
| WHERE sensitive_events > 5
| SORT sensitive_events DESC
| LIMIT 20
